newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea to raise Korea Fund's capital by $200 mln.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea to raise Korea Fund's capital by $200 mln.

text.p: South Korea's finance ministry said on Tuesday it would increase the Korea Fund's paid-in capital by $200 million in May to $580 million.
The ministry said in a statement the move was aimed at attracting foreign funds into the sagging Seoul stock market.
The ministry also said paid-in capital of the Korea Europe Fund and the Korea Asia Fund would be increased by about $100 million each during the second half of this year.
The Korea Europe Fund is capitalised at $240 million and the Korea Asia Fund at $200 million, the ministry said.
It also said it would allow the three country funds to buy stocks in the issuing market on a limited basis.
Currently, 20 percent of stocks offered for public subscription are allocated to institutions. The ministry said the country funds would be treated as institutions.
